newsitem.title: USA: Dow climbs higher, NYSE sets curbs.
newsitem.headline: Dow climbs higher, NYSE sets curbs.

text.p: The Dow industrial average scaled to greater heights on Friday, assisted by weak Producer Price Index (PPI) data.
The New York Stock Exchange set trading curbs after the Dow rose about 65 points to 7776 in late morning trading. The Nasdaq composite made a modest push higher, gaining about three points to 1414.

The PPI fell 0.3 percent in May. Economists had expected a 0.1 percent increase in the number. The decline supported the conventioanl wisdom that the Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates at its July meeting.
"Treasuries are up on a May PPI drop...signs of a slowing economy are really raising hopes that the Fed won't raise rates in July," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
The 30-year long bond was up 18/32 at a 6.73 percent yield. The Standard & Poor's futures index rose 6.5 points to 901.6.
Analysts said they expect the market to move steadily higher today though investors may opt to take profits later in the day.
